Appearance:
Shri N.S. Pal- learned counsel for the appellant/claimant.
Shri R.P. Gupta -Advocate for respondent No.2.

Shri Arvind Kumar Agarwal, learned counsel for the respondent 
 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 01.12.2012 passed by Fourteenth MACT, District-Gwalior (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.139/2011 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation and exonerating insurance company from the liability.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the case of injury of claimant, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.17,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.
Appellant received so many injuries in the accident and much money has been spent in his treatment.

So seeking enhancement of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17052 2 MA-292-2013 compensation to the tune of Rs. One Lac.
He further submits that Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error in exonerating the Insurance Company.
It is further submitted that it is true that at the time of the accident owner of offending vehicle has no permit to ply on the route of the accident but claimant is a third party.

So, it is the duty of the Hanni Singh Grover vs Pooran Singh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106872616/

sentences.text: Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount first to the claimant and then, recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the Claims Tribunal committed a grave error in totally exonerating the Insurance Company.
Therefore, it is prayed that compensation amount be enhanced and just and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company contended that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no enhancement.
He supported the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of the accident to ply on the route.
So, it is clear that it is a breach of policy and it is found proved that claimant is a third party.
This finding has not been challenged by the owner who is present before this Court.
So finding of the Tribunal in this regard is kept intact.
In view of the above, pay and recover policy must apply.
Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error in exonerating Insurance Company totally.
Therefore, the finding of the Claims Tribunal in this regard is set aside.
It is directed that the Insurance Company should satisfy the award in favour of the claimant firstly and then recover from owner and driver of the offending vehicle as per "pay and recover policy".

Since the Claims Tribunal awarded just Rs. 17,000/- as compensation, however, looking to the injuries, age and earning and future prospect of the claimant, it would be appropriate to enhance the award of compensation by a lump sum amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17052 3 MA-292-2013 Rs.50,000/-.
8. Accordingly, present appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove.
The amount of compensation is enhanced to a lump sum amount of Rs.50,000/- in the present appeal.
The appellant is entitled to receive the lump sum amount of Rs.50,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

9. The present appeal stands disposed of.
